papers.title_en: Chronic Pain Severity Modifies Gait Biomechanics and Muscle Activation in Individuals with Chronic Ankle Instability.
papers.title_zh: 慢性疼痛严重程度改变慢性踝关节不稳患者的步态生物力学和肌肉激活
papers.tldr_en: Individuals with CAI who report greater pain severity demonstrate distinct, time-specific gait deviations and greater neuromuscular inhibition, which may extend beyond the effects of instability alone.
papers.abstract_en:
PURPOSE
To investigate differences in neuromechanics during walking between individuals with chronic ankle instability (CAI) reporting high and low chronic pain, and healthy controls, with a focus on stance-phase joint kinematics and muscle activation patterns.


METHODS
Sixty physically active participants were classified into three groups: CAI with high pain (n=20), CAI with low pain (n=20), and controls (n=20). Pain severity was determined using the Foot and Ankle Outcome Score pain subscale. Three-dimensional lower extremity kinematics and surface electromyography activation of six lower extremity muscles were recorded during overground walking at self-selected speed. Functional data analysis was used to identify stance-phase differences between groups.

papers.abstract_en: Quantitatively deciphering the relationship between muscle activation and thickness deformation is essential for diagnosing muscle-related diseases and monitoring muscle health (e.g., Facioscapulohumeral Dystrophy). Despite the potential of ultrasound (US) imaging and sensing to measure changes in muscle thickness during movements, it remains challenging to make a fully portable device, considering the wiring and data collection. On the other hand, surface electromyography (sEMG) can record muscle bioelectrical signals and measure muscle activations, offering a unique perspective that correlates with underlying changes in muscle thickness. This paper introduces a deep-learning-based approach that used sEMG signals to infer muscle deformation. Using a hierarchical combination of self-attention and cross-attention mechanisms, this method predicted muscle deformation directly from sEMG data

papers.title_en: Effects of unilateral and bilateral eccentric training on lower limb maximal strength, jump, and sprint performance in trained adolescent male basketball players: a randomized controlled trial
papers.title_zh: 单侧和双侧离心训练对训练有素的青少年男性篮球运动员下肢最大力量、跳跃和冲刺表现的影响：一项随机对照试验
papers.journal: BMC Sports Science Medicine and Rehabilitation
papers.journal_tier: 康复医学2区/运动科学3区
papers.tldr_en: Although both UET and BET interventions demonstrated within-group potential to improve specific sports performance metrics in trained adolescent basketball players, neither modality established a statistically significant absolute between-group advantage.
papers.abstract_en: Basketball requires a solid foundation of lower limb strength and explosive power. Unilateral and bilateral resistance training modes may differ in improving sport-specific performance, but their relative effects and potential advantages in trained adolescent athletes remain unclear. This pilot study aims to explore the application effects of these two methods on specific performance indicators. This exploratory study aimed to compare the effects of a seven-week unilateral eccentric training (UET) and bilateral eccentric training (BET) on lower limb maximal strength, jump, and sprint performance in trained adolescent male basketball players. Twelve participants (n=12) were randomly assigned to either a UET or BET group. papers.title_en: Clinical applications of wearable sensor-based gait analysis in athletes: a systematic review for injury prevention and rehabilitation
papers.title_zh: 基于可穿戴传感器的步态分析在运动员临床应用中的作用：一项关于损伤预防与康复的系统综述
papers.journal: BMC Sports Science Medicine and Rehabilitation
papers.journal_tier: 康复医学2区/运动科学3区
papers.tldr_en: Evaluating the clinical efficacy of wearable sensor–based gait analysis for injury prevention in athletes, examining its role in rehabilitation monitoring and clinical decision-making, and identifying methodological limitations and future research priorities required for standardized clinical integration identifies key challenges.
papers.abstract_en: Gait analysis is fundamental for optimizing athletic performance and mitigating injury risks in sports medicine. While traditional laboratory assessments offer insights, the emergence of wearable sensor technology provides novel opportunities for objective, real-time gait evaluation in ecologically valid settings. This systematic review aims to (1) evaluate the clinical efficacy of wearable sensor–based gait analysis for injury prevention in athletes (2), examine its role in rehabilitation monitoring and clinical decision-making, and (3) identify methodological limitations and future research priorities required for standardized clinical integration. Adhering to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase from inception to May 31st, 2025. papers.title_en: Effects of different dietary supplements combined with conditioning training on muscle strength, jump performance, sprint speed, and muscle mass in athletes: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
papers.title_zh: 不同膳食补充剂结合体能训练对运动员肌肉力量、跳跃表现、冲刺速度和肌肉质量的影响：一项系统综述和网络荟萃分析
papers.tldr_en: Protein supplementation appears to be the most effective strategy for increasing muscular strength; β-alanine and creatine both improve jump performance, with β-alanine offering marginally superior effectiveness; and creatine is particularly beneficial for sprint speed.
papers.abstract_en: Background As dietary supplements have become integral to meeting athletes’ specialised nutritional requirements, research into their effects on performance has intensified. Yet inconsistent findings leave the efficacy of some supplements—most notably branched-chain amino acids and β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB)—open to debate. To clarify which products offer the greatest benefit, we undertook a systematic review and network meta-analysis aimed at identifying the supplements most effective for athletes, including protein, creatine, β-alanine, HMB, vitamin D, caffeine, and others. Methods PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, Embase and SPORTDiscus were searched from database inception to 15 March 2024 for RCTs evaluating the effects of dietary supplements (including but not limited to protein, creatine, β-alanine, HMB, caffeine, and vitamin D) on athletic performance. papers.abstract_zh: 背景：由于膳食补充剂已成为满足运动员特殊营养需求不可或缺的一部分，对其性能影响的研究也随之加剧。然而，不一致的研究结果使得某些补充剂（最著名的是支链氨基酸和β-羟基-β-甲基丁酸酯 (HMB)）的功效仍存在争议。为了明确哪些产品能带来最大益处，我们进行了一项系统综述和网络荟萃分析，旨在确定对运动员最有效的补充剂，包括蛋白质、肌酸、β-丙氨酸、HMB、维生素D、咖啡因等。方法：发布...

papers.title_en: Building for the Future: A Systematic Review of the Effects of Eccentric Resistance Training on Measures of Physical Performance in Youth Athletes
papers.title_zh: 展望未来：一项关于离心抗阻训练对青少年运动员身体表现指标影响的系统综述
papers.tldr_en: The findings of this systematic review support the inclusion of eccentric resistance training in youth athletes to improve measures of muscular strength, jump, sprint and change of direction performance.
papers.abstract_en: Background Eccentric resistance training is recognised as an effective stimulus for enhancing measures of muscular strength and power in adult populations; however, its value in youth athletes is currently not well understood. Objective The aim of this systematic review was to critically appraise the effects of eccentric resistance training on measures of physical performance (i.e. muscular strength, jump, sprint and change of direction) in youth athletes 18 years of age and under. Methods Original journal articles published between 1950 and June 2022 were retrieved from electronic search engines of PubMed, SPORTDiscus and Google Scholar’s advanced search option.
